annotationRationale: Absolute value determines the allowed distances, and the integer endpoints determine the count. The equivalent shared-bank method fully resolves this short problem; another method would repeat the same reasoning.

classificationReview.areaRationale: The central task is an absolute-value inequality and its integer solutions, so Algebra is more appropriate than Counting & Probability.
classificationReview.areaCheck: The recommendation to change the area to Algebra is an obvious correct repair because the central task is an absolute-value inequality and its integer solutions.

review.questionCheck: Since 9<3π<10, the integer solutions are −9 through 9, totaling 19, choice D. The supplied equivalent 2021_AMC_10B_Q01 statement, choices and key agree. No figures are supplied.
review.alternativeMethodCheck: 2021_AMC_10B_Q01#count-integer-distances is retained and independently verified. The reference interval-counting and positive-negative-pair arguments are equivalent for this short problem; another route would add little learner value.
review.annotationCheck: Both assessed IDs match the task: absolute value as distance and counting integer solutions of an inequality. Empty support and context lists are reasonable.
review.areaCheck: The recommendation to change the area to Algebra is an obvious correct repair because the central task is an absolute-value inequality and its integer solutions.

methodReviews.mathCheck: The allowed integer distances are exactly 0 through 9. Each of the nine positive distances gives two solutions, while zero gives one, so the total is 2·9+1=19. The strict endpoints are correctly respected.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: The candidate explicitly reuses amc/2021_AMC_10B_Q01#count-integer-distances. Both inherited references, live-reference-2021_AMC_10B_Q01 and aops-reference-2021_AMC_10B_Q01, are retained. The project prose and its source-informed-original provenance are correctly credited.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The distance interpretation motivates the first move, and the separate treatment of zero prevents the main counting error. The approximation clearly locates the integer endpoints.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: cnm_007 directly supports distance from zero and opposite-number pairs; cnm_h020 directly supports listing and counting the allowed integers.

nativeLayerJudgments.CN: Both exact CN topic links fit the explanation and the assessed roles.
nativeLayerJudgments.US: The narrower 6.NS.C.7 link and the distance component of partial 6.NS.C.7c fit. The partial 7.NS.A.1c and 6.NS.C.7d links add no substantive coverage here. cnm_h020 has no supplied US link.
nativeLayerJudgments.ailleo: Both immediate concepts are precise and sufficient for this elementary solution; no broader counting concept is needed.
